verification_report.summary:
Verified the full reconstruction in textual order through 17 structured statement checks. Every assertion and deduction passes under the stated distributional admissibility and lower-C2-test maximality hypotheses.

The algebraic identities for P_n, subharmonicity, convolution, convexity, and invariance are valid. Strictifying a lower touch proves stability under local uniform limits. The perturbed smooth comparison argument works on any bounded open set with the stated continuity on its closure; boundary regularity is unnecessary. The n=2 case reduces correctly to bounded plurisubharmonic functions. For n>=3, the H direct-sum 0 identity gives both weak and strict positivity equivalences, and non-strict lower touches allow maximality to descend.

Normalization and subharmonicity of v squared are justified. Radial probability averages increase by spherical submeans; the L1 translation estimate makes their limits independent of the center, and the submean inequality identifies both limits as 1. In Case 1, translated and unitarily rotated mollifications converge to the same Lipschitz maximal limit. Vanishing directional L2 energy gives independence of one complex coordinate. Induction then yields a constant c and the contradiction 4/3<=1-c<=1. Negating this case gives exactly the stated uniform energy quantifiers.

The numerical choice v(0)<1/12 is sufficient: 2v(0)<1/6 while the sum of the two averages minus 4/3 exceeds 1/6. For fixed rho and r, remove an annulus whose energy is at most half of E=C_rho^{-1}. If m>0 is the kernel minimum on the remaining closed ball, then B_epsilon>=mE I uniformly in position, direction, and small epsilon. Nonnegativity of v_epsilon and linearity give P_n(A_epsilon)>=0. Subtracting cI with 0<c<=mE preserves admissibility, and fixed-radius convolution gives convergence in every derivative. The resulting D' contains 0, lies in D, satisfies c|z|^2<2/3, and has h=v on its boundary. Smooth comparison supplies the final contradiction.

The reference and its open-versus-closed cone definitions were verified against [Szekelyhidi, Theorem 20 and Sections 5-6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.02762v3), using web fallback after the theorem-search tool timed out. The reconstruction independently supplies the weighted-kernel argument and the sufficient numerical choice. No Cartan black box, nonlinear PDE estimate, or STW existence theorem is needed. All hypotheses have their required roles. The final remark about bounded subharmonicity alone is correct and only contextual.
